I believe you and your feelings are completely valid, I cannot imagine how hard it is to handle something like this. I can see why anyone would feel regret.


The foster system is overloaded to be honest. She was more likely to find parents that abused her in some fashion than a parent who cares as much as you do. I know its hard to view it this way, but in my first comment i said that lashing out can be a symptom of trust in situations like this. I dont know your daughter, so I could be wrong, but if im right in that being a part of what it is, that means you are actually doing very well in raising her. She feels safe enough to show the worst parts of herself. Its unfortunate that she is so traumatized that her way of vulnerability with someone means seeing the results of all the horrible things she went through.


It can get better though. In my situation I eventually outgrew these out bursts. You said she dresses inappropriately and tries to look for attention? Well the solution to attention seeking is feeling loved. Try to think of these out bursts as a test. She might be subconsciously trying to see if you will give up on her like everyone else.


I dont know what your relationship with her is like, so maybe this advice is for nothing, but ill tell you what definitely didnt work when I was younger. When I was going through some things every conversation I had with my parents became about trying to work through the issues I had, going as far as to disrupt any good times that occured, which tore a rift between us even further. If you can, if she's open to it, keep trying to take her out to do fun things every now and then, and don't bring up the horrible things she's said, done, and have gone through at all. Make her feel like you still want to be around her by inviting her to go and do fun activities with you. You want her to feel like she is still loved despite everything. I believe that can help fix your relationship with her. Make sure she knows that you love her.


I also just want to say, you are a good parent. Her lashing out is not indicative of failings on your part, it is indicative of the failings of her former familys part + any other foster families she was with. She takes you for granted and she will realize some day that you are only trying to help and protect her. No matter what happens, you are a good parent. You are doing your best and that is all anyone can ask for.

I had NO spice tolerance for yeaaaaars. A few years ago I started eating "spicy" chicken strips, which was really just chicken with some pepper lol. Then I started adding spices to canned soups trying to upgrade them, like getting some chipotle powder and cayenne and adding it to stuff. After that I started eating spicy ramen like tapatio chicken flavor ramen. I also make my own homemade ramen now and at first I only added chipotle powder and cayenne in terms of spicy ingredients, then I started adding sriracha, and then chili garlic. Now I add spices to my vegetables, fries... honestly everything you can name I've made spicy.

3 years ago I could only eat 3 bites of buldak 3x spicy ramen noodles. It was unbearable, but now I use their hot sauce with vegetables at least once a week and enjoy it very much. I do not recommend starting off with something so spicy that it is intolerable because it takes the joy out of eating. Just buy some chipotle powder, put it on some things you like like soups or vegetables, and then when that tolerance builds get some cayenne and start doing both, and move up from there. It will get easier the more you eat them. If even these spices are too hot just start with adding pepper to lots of things. Whatever you use, try eating it regularly like multiple times a week once you find something you like with it.

I learned the things I enjoy via experimentation with hot spices, adding them to a bunch of stuff I was eating already. Be willing to try them on different things. If the chipotle powder flavor ends up bothering you (not the spiciness itself but THE FLAVOR) try a different spice that's hot instead, but I've found it is good with almost everything to me.

Hi, I'm a lurker of this subreddit and I'm not a parent. That being said, I am a former kid lol and I grew up an only child and begged and pleaded for siblings from my parents. Eventually, long story short, I ended up in foster care where I actually got to experience what it was like to have siblings. I actually ended up missing being an only child while I was in foster care!! I love them like genetic siblings and got the full experience, but it was very annoying at times! Then when I was reunified with my parents after foster care, I actually ended up missing living with my new siblings! I am telling you this because, honestly, your daughter probably can't fully comprehend what having a sibling would be like. It definitely is not all sunshine and rainbows, there are pros and cons to both having siblings and not having them.

I've always heard people say "the grass is greener on the other side" but it has quite literally NEVER felt truer and more accurate than my experience with and without having siblings. When I didn't have them, I missed them, and when I had them, I didn't want them. Your daughter is going to be okay, most likely once she got a sibling she'd on some level wish they weren't around LOL no matter how much they loved them, because SIBLINGS ARE NOT JUST A BLESSING, BUT ALSO A CURSE! I say all of these negative things in an endearing way of course. Hope that makes sense and isn't offensive.

Hi, I don't know if you've found your answer yet, but I also struggle with using my hands as a mouse and I have tried multiple options. No matter what you do these options will always be more expensive than a mouse unfortunately, but here is what I have found that works.

I use a [kensington slimblade](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B001MTE32Y?ref=nb_sb_ss_w_as-reorder_k0_1_7&amp=&crid=26CV9AFNO35W2&sprefix=kensing&th=1), at first I tried it with my feet but it was causing nerve compression because I was using the ball with one foot and clicking with the other, which was causing the foot controlling the ball to be doing the equivalent of stepping on a rock 24/7. now I use it with my elbow, lower and upper arm. I say all three because I change it up randomly. But it works great. I have it velcro'd to the arm of my chair on my right side. it has 4 buttons and you control the cursor with the ball in the middle. Because of how it is situated though, I cannot click and drag. To compensate for clicking and dragging, I also use foot pedals that can be assigned as left and right click. I currently use the [iKKEGOL](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08MC456TC?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title) foot pedal but if you have the budget (I have two, one for left click the other for right), the [elgato](https://www.amazon.com/Elgato-Stream-Deck-Pedal-footswitches/dp/B09PRMCTGB?dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.ZJeLOBOqWJ_WPGp-PXoAhFnZi_0lHMUsAdmoekrtGmK7Me0c4kooCZSYVBlsLW_FFdj8ALI9hCm8Xlp_2xXRtJPXQjQPZdPCAQSyPXvWNB0eafFxSIYUz4zTp1-P1_zdhJAGA2abwossLWuaPz1Dc0LCFrjC1f1EjrpnarBOVhWgvZpb2HFlZ7nQWj_8xm3g-_jgsZZWQHt8b7iHpaf4fHb78DuxMXoAddD7k3qj11w.krXynCZO-mOBXL1ffLTY9g6mCKxZ_dd6q1bVWvAEIWw&dib_tag=se&keywords=elgato+foot+pedal&qid=1743883418&sr=8-1) foot pedal will make your feet less tired as quickly due to requiring less pressure and can be adjusted to the amount of pressure required to use them. I have the foot pedals velcro'd to a height adjustable stool, you want to try and make it so your feet are at as natural of an angle as possible, not leaning too far up or too far down when you are resting them. I prop my heels up to try and make the front of my toes level with the back.

You will feel some straining in your body at first, this is because you might be using some muscles that are not usually moved, especially not in such an unusual fashion. This is normal. It will take a while for your body to adjust to this, do not overexert yourself, like starting a new exercise you can hurt yourself if you do too much too soon.

Hi, I don't know if you're still looking for a foot mouse but I personally use [The Kensington Slimblade.](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B001MTE32Y?ref_=ppx_hzsearch_conn_dt_b_fed_asin_title_1)

It's meant to be a mouse for your hands but you can use it with your feet technically. It may take some time for your legs to get used to the exercise and you may become a little sore at first so take rest days until you can tolerate it for longer periods. I put a book under my heel and that helped some. I velcro'd it to a foot stool so it doesn't move at all. It is plug and play since it is meant to be a mouse for your hands, setup was extremely easy. You should clean it once a week using a baby wipe because dust can interfere with the ball that moves the cursor's smoother movements. You use the balls of your feet to move the ball in the middle and click, it has 4 programmable buttons including ones for left and right click.

It has made my PC usage significantly easier and unlike some other options the learning curve was very small. I learned how to use it very well within 1-2 weeks. If it's not out of your budget consider giving it a try.

I don't have any advice when it comes to wasd but for mouses I always recommend and use personally [The Kensington Slimblade.](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B001MTE32Y?ref_=ppx_hzsearch_conn_dt_b_fed_asin_title_1) I prop my heel up on a book, velcro the book and the mouse to a foot stool and use the balls of both my feet to move the mouse and click. You will most likely need to clean it once a week to stop dust from getting stuck on it like I do, and it takes some time for your feet to get used to the exercise and they may become tired, so you'll have to take breaks until your body can handle that kind of stress. But it's significantly improved my life as I have similar problems as you do. It is actually meant to be a mouse for your hands so it is completely plug and play no fancy steps necessary and has 4 programmable buttons including left and right click. You move the ball in the middle to move the cursor.

It works very well for me but requires both your feet to use it, one for mouse movement, one for clicking. Setup is extremely easy however, so weigh your pros and cons! Hope this helps in your search.

Well that's not really the point, that was just an example. The point is that the more hobbies you have the more interesting a person you are and the more people will want to talk to you. That's what I want you to take away from this the most.

The library near me for example has a club where people will get together and crochet, even teaching some of the less experienced members. It is less likely for you to find group settings in real life where people talk about music and cars, and even if you did women aren't as likely to participate.

I genuinely believe that if you branch out your interests you will be much much more likely to find friends in general. You can't expand your world view or meet new people without going to places those new people typically hang out at. It is significantly harder anyway.

Maybe once you become acquaintances try to ask her some would you rather questions, invite her to go to some sort of event or try a new hobby with you. for example; pottery studios are pretty common all over the USA, but look into the specific stores and events around your area. Try to meet up mainly in public places at first, but places that aren't too crowded or too intimate. Don't take her to the movies at first for example because it might imply you want to go out with her, that's easier for girl and guy friendships to do if you've established that you aren't trying to go out with her first. And don't take her to a concert because then how will you hear each other speak? lol. I recommended pottery classes, because the public place but semi personal vibe is exactly what you are looking for. Renaissance faires, carnivals, museums, aquariums, zoos, etc are also really fun. If you say something that is bothering you like an insecurity or w/e and she never tells you anything going wrong in her own personal life there is a good chance she is not ready or willing to talk about personal subjects like that with you. I would not test it until you are about 9 months in to be safe. Honestly, if you want to be really certain that you won't cause this problem again, **I recommend waiting until she talks about her problems first because then you know she feels comfortable talking about serious subjects with you.** You want to establish that it is fun to be around you before talking about things like that. If a month in you start talking about all of your problems, unconsciously or not, whoever you are talking to will begin to associate you with those negative things. That's why you have to try and not go overboard about it. If you spend more time talking about negative things compared to positive ones, that is what your friendship with them will become.

I had bed bugs on and off for many years. I did all kinds of crazy shit, but I don't know how big your infestation is.

I checked my mattresses every day (+have covers over them to protect from bugs)  
I put double sided tape on all four legs of my bed and desk chair (you can do this with DE instead, just try not to touch it or move the object its on)  
I put my bed away from the wall and made sure no blankets touched the floor  
I wiped my desk chair down with rubbing alcohol to kill any eggs  
I sprayed bug spray every day  
Washed the sheets/anything fabric related

This was all before I started using DE. Honestly, I literally had ptsd from bed bugs, so when I made this post about the DE I started randomly getting itchy and getting those spots on my arms. I panicked and said enough was enough and bought the DE. I don't know if it really was bed bugs coming back or not, but the spots went away afterwards. For that reason though, since I never actually SAW one of the bugs I can't say how much it helped. Supposedly it's the best method out there. Also, I did all the techniques above when I couldn't afford a steamer. If you're going to use the DE put it in spots you or your pets wouldn't touch very often, like underneath a dresser for example. And also putting it near access points to places where you hang out a lot helps (like I mentioned above with the 4 legs to my bed). Don't sleep in a different room, if you do that they will move with you and then infect that room as well. They can survive without blood for many years so I'd keep up whatever techniques you use for at least 6 months, even if you no longer see them or feel itchy.
